story_title: [TEST ONLY — not a real story] V17 grammar stress test — every remaining path
alt_text_per_slide: Slide 1: 94% of breaches start with one email.. Not a zero-day. Not malware. A single click. — shown as a grid of cells showing the proportion as filled versus empty cells.
Slide 2: How one click becomes a full compromise.. Click — credential capture — session token stolen — internal network — lateral movement — full compromise. — shown as a diagram of connected steps.
Slide 3: The layers a request has to pass through.. Client — API gateway — auth layer — application server — database. — shown as a diagram of connected steps.

Slide 4: The startup spent $2,400,000 chasing the wrong fix.. They spent every dollar on the wrong patch and had nothing to show for it — new firewall — pen test contract — compliance audit — breach anyway. — shown as a row of blocks that shrink to show a resource being spent down.

Slide 5: How fast this category actually grew.. In 2019 it was a research paper. By 2021 the first commercial product shipped. In 2023 every major cloud vendor added native support. By 2025 it was the industry default. — shown as a timeline with dated points.
Slide 6: The evidence trail nobody followed up on.. A quiet commit changed the auth check. — shown as pinned reference facts.
Slide 7: Patched vs unpatched systems, six months later.. The gap compounds faster than most teams expect. — shown as a side-by-side comparison.

Slide 8: Everyone thinks bigger companies are safer targets to avoid.. Actually, attackers prefer them — more third-party vendors means more doors. — shown as a common misconception struck through, with the correct answer stated below it.
Slide 9: Security is a habit, not a product. — shown as one large highlighted number or word.
Slide 10: One click is still the whole story.. Save this before your team needs it. — shown as a closing statement with the GetByteRush signature.
